name: PT Metropolitan Land Tbk

frontmatter.title: Metropolitan Land: a good township developer at a full price
frontmatter.summary: MTLA is a well-run Bekasi township developer with a mall and hotel arm, a clean balance sheet and a record of paying dividends. The land is carried at cost and the business is worth about book value, but the shares have re-rated to a premium to their own four-year multiples. We initiate at REDUCE.
thesis: Marketing sales of 1,875 IDR bn in FY2025 came in just under target; the 2026 target is 2,000 IDR bn, and 9M2026 marketing sales of 1,420 IDR bn were about seven tenths of it, so the plan is reachable but not beatable [S3][S4].

Reported 9M2026 revenue rose to 1,178 IDR bn but net profit to parent fell to 183 IDR bn as gross margin slipped and other gains shrank; our FY2026E parent profit of 379.5 is below the company's own guided growth [S4][S6].
RNAV per share is close to book value per share because land enters at audited cost and the malls are capitalised on a yield basis; there is no hidden revaluation surplus to unlock.

At Rp700 the shares trade at 14.1x FY2026E earnings against a four-year range whose top it has now passed, and at 0.9x book against a band it has left behind; the re-rating, not the fundamentals, is the story.
Our target of Rp519 implies -24.5% total return; the dividend, at a payout capped near a fifth of profit, does not bridge the gap.

catalysts.event: FY2026 results and the 2027 marketing-sales target
Expiry of the property VAT incentive (PPN DTP) that has supported house sales in 2026
AGM and the FY2026 dividend decision

blocks.text: **REDUCE, target Rp519, -24.5% total return.** MTLA is the Bekasi township developer behind Metland Menteng, Metland Transyogi, Metland Cibitung and Metland Cyber Puri, with four shopping centres and a small hotel group attached. It is a decent business: gross margin held at 52.8% through a down year, net debt is IDR544.4bn against EBITDA of IDR648.5bn, and the company has paid a dividend every year since listing [S7]. The problem is the price. At Rp700 the shares sit at 0.9x book and 14.1x our FY2026E earnings, above the top of the four-year range on both measures, while the asset base that backs them is worth about book value on our RNAV.

The variant view is narrow and it is about the multiple, not the business. The market is paying for a recovery in marketing sales that the company itself only guides at mid-single-digit growth for 2026, and for a margin recovery that 9M2026 does not show: revenue rose to 1,178 IDR bn but gross profit fell to 556 IDR bn and net profit to parent fell to 183 IDR bn [S6]. We think FY2026 parent profit lands near IDR379.5bn, below the level the company targeted for 2025 and below the growth it guided for 2026 [S4].

What moves the value, in order: the marketing-sales run-rate against the 2,000 IDR bn target, the BI path (mortgage affordability transmits with a two-to-three quarter lag), and the discount to RNAV, which is where most of the debate sits. A return to the wide end of the sector's discount band would take the shares far lower; holding the current premium requires the re-rating to be structural, and the free float of 20.7% alongside insider ownership of 83.8% argues that it is liquidity, not a change in the economics, that has driven the shares up from the 410.0 low [S0].

MTLA develops and sells residential townships, shop-houses, land plots, apartments and offices, and runs the commercial property it retains. The audited segment note splits the group four ways: real estate, shopping centres, hotels and other (recreation and sports centres) [S7 note 34]. In FY2025 real estate produced 1,251.6 of revenue and shopping centres 360.3, with the balance in hotels and other; total revenue was 1,780.5 [S7]. The development line is the swing factor: it fell in FY2025 while mall rent rose and hotels were flat, which is the standard shape of a township developer's P&L when handovers slow [S7].

The business model is land-led. MTLA buys large parcels on the eastern and southern edge of Jakarta - Bekasi, Cibitung, Cikarang, Cileungsi, Transyogi - installs infrastructure and sells plots and build-to-order houses in phases, retaining the commercial nodes as malls and hotels. That produces a high gross margin because the land was bought years before the sale, and it produces a large inventory balance: real-estate inventory of IDR3,271bn current and IDR1,028bn non-current on the audited balance sheet, plus group operating working capital of IDR2,970bn against revenue of IDR1,780bn. Operating working capital is the group figure, not the real-estate inventory line, and property and equipment is a further IDR839bn [S7]. It also means the balance sheet, not the P&L, is where the value sits.

The retained commercial portfolio is the stabiliser. Four malls (Grand Metropolitan and Metropolitan Mall Bekasi, Plaza Tambun, Mall Metropolitan Cileungsi) plus apartments and offices produced 360.3 of rent in FY2025 and a positive segment result after allocated marketing, administration and final tax [S7]. Hotels are the weak spot: 112 IDR bn of 9M2026 revenue but a negative segment result in FY2025, which is why we treat the recurring block as the malls alone [S6][S7].

Strategy is the company's own: launch in strategic locations in Greater Jakarta, keep the commercial component to support land values, and hold debt below a stated ceiling. Management targets marketing sales growth in the mid single digits and revenue growth in the low teens for 2026, with net profit up modestly, a capital structure inside its stated ceiling and a dividend of up to a fifth of net profit [S4]. The dividend policy is unchanged for 2026 [S4].

MTLA is a challenger, not a leader. It competes with the BSD, Summarecon and Ciputra townships for the same eastern-Jakarta homebuyer and with the listed retail landlords for tenants, and its scale is a fraction of theirs. The company was established in 1994 and is domiciled in Bekasi [S4]. The controlling shareholder holds 83.8% of the shares on the vendor's count and turnover is thin: average daily value traded over three months was 632,735,587.3 [S0].

The Metland brand is best known in Bekasi, where the group built its earliest townships and where the
founding family still controls it through a private holding vehicle. Township development on the
eastern edge of Jakarta is a land-banking business: the developer buys raw land before infrastructure
arrives, funds the trunk infrastructure, and sells serviced plots and houses at a multiple of land
cost. The model is capital-hungry in the early phases and cash-generative once a township matures,
which is why the balance sheet alternates between land purchases and handover-driven cash receipts.

Indonesian residential property is a volume business with a policy lever attached. The relevant demand drivers are mortgage rates, the VAT incentive on landed houses (PPN DTP), real income growth and consumer confidence; the relevant supply constraint is land in the Jakarta corridors [S4]. MTLA's own annual report describes 2025 as a year in which demand shifted down-price: sales of small houses held up, mid and large units were under pressure, and rental demand for commercial space softened while selling prices for commercial property rose [S4]. The company responded by shifting from retail-unit selling to selling commercial lots and by re-targeting its hotel business from government to corporate accounts [S4].

Policy is the swing factor in 2026. The property tax incentive has been the support under house sales this year, and MTLA says it will optimise it through year-end [S3]. Its expiry at the end of 2026 is the cleanest dated risk in the story, and it is also why 9M2026 marketing sales of 1,420 IDR bn reached about seven tenths of the 2,000 IDR bn target rather than running at the target's pace [S3].

The rate backdrop is not helpful. The house macro deck has the policy rate at 5.75% through the forecast, CPI at 3.28% and the rupiah at Rp18,350/USD against the dollar from a spot Rp17,968/USD [deck: macro][S0]. These are the deck's own values and the model uses the same deck for the cost of capital and the market rate, so section two, section five and the model share one path. For a developer that sells on mortgage affordability, a flat policy rate and a soft currency is a headwind to volume and a support to replacement cost - which is exactly the mix that keeps nominal prices up and transaction volumes down.

Competitive position: MTLA is a specialist in the eastern Jakarta corridor with a small but real moat in land. Its townships are established, the infrastructure is in, and the land was acquired cheaply, so the development margin (52.8% in a down year) is structurally above what a late entrant could earn. The moat does not extend to pricing power, and the company has no scale advantage in procurement or in access to capital. Five forces, briefly: rivalry is high and localised; buyer power is high because the homebuyer compares estates on price and access; supplier power is moderate (contractors are plentiful, land sellers in the corridor are not); new entrants are constrained by land availability in the established corridors but not elsewhere; substitutes are rental housing and secondary stock, which are close substitutes at the affordable end [S7]. The net effect is a business that earns a decent return on land it already owns and a poor return on new land bought at today's prices.

Relative to the other names we cover in the sector, MTLA sits between the pure township developers and the mall-backed developers [S0]: it has CTRA's land-led margin profile at a fraction of the scale, and PWON's recurring-income support at a fraction of the rent roll. We cover CBDK at SELL, JRPT at HOLD, CTRA at BUY and PWON at BUY; MTLA's issue is not the sector view but its own valuation against its own history.

The Indonesian government has used property tax incentives repeatedly since the pandemic, cutting VAT on
eligible landed houses for limited windows and extending them when transaction volumes fell. Developers
in the Jakarta suburbs typically report a burst of sales in the final weeks of an incentive window, so a
strong marketing-sales quarter is not by itself evidence of underlying demand. The listed developers
also differ widely in how much of their land bank they have already monetised: a mature township with
infrastructure is worth several times an equally sized raw parcel in a district without access roads,
which is why RNAV work on this sector is really a land-valuation exercise.

Revenue fell from 2,020.8 in FY2024 to 1,780.5 in FY2025 as handovers slowed, but gross margin held at 52.8% and EBITDA, restated for the true depreciation charge, was 648.5 [S7]. The line the data pack gets wrong is depreciation: it carries 97.7 after our restatement against the small administrative share the pack shows, because most of the charge sits in cost of revenue (investment-property depreciation) and in direct costs, not in administrative expenses [S7]. The same is true of finance cost: the P&L line is 6.0, but the cash finance cost paid was many times that and the rest is capitalised into inventory, which is part of why development margin looks as high as it does [S7].

Nine-month revenue of 1,178 IDR bn was up on 9M2025, but gross profit slipped to 556 IDR bn and parent net profit fell to 183 IDR bn [S6]. Management guided double-digit revenue growth and modest net profit growth for 2026 [S4]; on the nine-month run-rate neither is achievable without a very strong fourth quarter. We model FY2026E revenue of IDR1,685.3bn and parent profit of IDR379.5bn, EPS of 49.6 against 53.9 in FY2025. The arithmetic is explicit: the implied fourth quarter is FY2026E parent profit of IDR379.5bn less the nine-month actual of IDR182.6bn, set against the FY2025 fourth quarter of IDR412.9bn less IDR232.5bn. So the base needs a fourth quarter above last year's, not a repeat of it, and it is not an annualisation of the nine-month rate either. That recovery is the most likely path, not an optimistic one: marketing sales of IDR1,420bn were already well into the IDR2,000bn target at nine months [S3], the company is optimising the PPN DTP incentive through year-end [S3], and the fourth quarter is seasonally the strongest handover quarter in its own record [S4]. The company's own record supports that shape: FY2025 net profit of IDR412.9bn came in short of target, with revenue and marketing sales also below plan [S4].

A note on the model's revenue line. The template carries two revenue buckets - development and recurring - and we map them to the real-estate and shopping-centre segments. Hotel revenue (112 IDR bn in 9M2026) and other revenue therefore sit outside the modelled line. The red team is right that this cannot be treated as free: those two segments produced a combined result of minus a small amount in FY2025, but their gross profit was not zero [S7 note 34]. We therefore charge operating cost on the same scope as the revenue - group SG&A of 389.4 less the hotel and other segments' allocated share derived from the segment note, which is 18.4% of modelled revenue - and carry the below-EBIT recurring charge (final tax, the joint venture's loss, other gains) separately at -61.5 [S7]. On that definition the model's FY2025 EBIT reconciles to the audited P&L plus the removed segments' small loss, instead of understating it by the hotel and other gross profit as the previous draft's "EBIT is unaffected" claim implied. The same correction means the FY2026E P/E quoted elsewhere is on the corrected EPS.

Costs. SG&A on the modelled scope is 389.4 in FY2025 and we hold the ratio at 18.4% of revenue [S7]. The consolidated nine-month SG&A of the group is higher because it includes the hotel and other cost bases, which is why a group ratio is not the comparison. The development gross margin is held at 55.0% because the land cost is sunk, but the red team is right that the reported margin fell: consolidated gross profit slipped to the 556 IDR bn level on 1,178 IDR bn in 9M2026, diluted by mix into lower-margin hotel and other revenue, and the development segment's own result fell to 128 IDR bn on 777 IDR bn from a much higher ratio a year earlier, after allocated SG&A and final tax [S6]. Margin pressure is therefore real at the operating line, and the five-point give-back sits in the bear case rather than being dismissed [S6].

Cash flow and the balance sheet are the constraint. Working capital is the line the red team was right about: the old model used the engine default for working capital against an actual FY2025 ratio that is materially higher, and the default manufactured a large working-capital release and net cash in FY2026E. We now set working capital at the last actual ratio (184.2% of modelled revenue), so the forecast absorbs cash as the company actually does: FY2026E free cash flow to the firm is 227.5, not the four-digit number the default produced, and net debt in FY2026E is 452.5 rather than net cash. That is still below the 30 September actual, because the model is built from the FY2025 year-end balance sheet; the nine-month accounts already show the absorption we now forecast, which is the honest read of the run-rate [S6]. Net debt was 544.4 at the FY2025 year-end; by 30 September 2026 the company had drawn bank loans of 1,297 IDR bn against cash of 395 IDR bn, lifting net debt well above the year-end level [S6]. Net borrowing is held flat because the last actual shows the loan stock almost unchanged over nine months, not because debt cannot rise.

**Interest cover.** The old text argued cover was comfortable because most interest is capitalised. That was a category error: capitalisation defers interest into inventory rather than removing it. On cash numbers, finance cost paid was 67.1 IDR bn in FY2025, against a shopping-centre segment result of 116 IDR bn [S7]. Recurring income covers cash interest with a thin margin, not a comfortable one, and a presales winter would be funded from the balance sheet rather than from the malls. That is a real constraint on the rating.

Capital allocation is conservative and predictable: a dividend of up to a fifth of net profit, the rest retained into land and construction [S4]. The FY2025 dividend was 9.7 per share, 0.2 of EPS, paid in June 2026 [S0]. There has been no rights issue and no buyback.
Earnings-quality flags, per the house screen:

items: **Accruals.** Non-financial, so the accrual ratio applies. The gap between parent profit of IDR412.9bn and free cash flow to the firm of IDR101.3bn is large and persistent, but it is explained by inventory: a developer recognises profit on handover and reinvests the cash in land in the same year, so we treat it as a business-model feature rather than a manipulation flag and monitor the advance book instead.

**Receivables.** Current trade receivables rose from IDR70.0bn at 31 December 2024 to IDR214.9bn at 31 December 2025 - more than tripled - while revenue growth was -11.9% over the same year [S7]. That divergence is the flag: it can precede a handover-driven revenue catch-up, but it can equally precede a collection problem, so it stays on the watch list until the 2026 collections show which it is.
**IDX regime.** No special-monitoring board, no special notation and no late filing in the FY2025 audited accounts or the 9M2026 report [S6][S7].
**Related parties.** Sales to related parties were immaterial against FY2025 revenue, and related-party payables are small [S7 note 33].

**Structure.** No pledged controlling stake disclosed, no serial rights issues and no auditor change identified in the filings we read [S7]. The risk here is concentration of ownership, not a structure flag: 83.8% insider ownership with a 20.7% float.

blocks.text: We value MTLA on RNAV first, with P/E and P/BV as cross-checks, at the industry weights: RNAV dominant, with P/E and P/BV as the minority checks. That is the right method set for a developer because the P&L describes handovers already contracted rather than the land still to be sold, and because the company's own history shows the shares trade on asset value and book rather than on earnings momentum.

**RNAV, component by component.** The land and development value is built from four balance-sheet lines, each a fact with a verbatim quote from the 30 September 2026 filing, so the asset side and the liabilities side of the RNAV sit on the same date: real-estate inventory, current portion, of 3,539 IDR bn - land under development, buildings under construction and buildings ready for sale [S6 note 7]; real-estate inventory, non-current portion, of 1,070 IDR bn - land not yet developed [S6 note 7]; property and equipment of 998 IDR bn, which is where the hotels and their equipment sit [S6]; less unearned revenue and customer advances of 265 IDR bn [S6 note 18]. That is the land-and-development value the engine uses. On the FY2025 audited balance sheet the same four lines total 3,271 IDR bn plus 1,028 IDR bn plus 839 IDR bn less 295 IDR bn [S7], and using that December base against September net debt was the inconsistency the QC auditor flagged: it understated the land block and therefore the RNAV leg. Investment properties are a separate balance-sheet line and are not double counted: the malls are valued through the cap rate below [S6].

No appraisal uplift and no haircut are taken. The method card asks for appraised value with a stated haircut; the only defensible number we can source is carrying cost, and an appraisal of Bekasi township land would be a promoter's number, so the land enters at what the company paid. The bull case carries the mark-up toward replacement cost instead. The shopping centres are valued by capitalising recurring gross profit at a cap rate equivalent to a normal net-property-income yield once mall overheads are deducted; hotels are excluded from that block because their segment result is negative, and they are inside property and equipment above [S7].

**One balance-sheet date in every leg.** Assets and liabilities are both struck at 30 September 2026, and every bridge deduction is now a September line rather than a June pack figure: the land block from the September inventory, property and equipment and advances facts above, then net debt of loans 1,297 IDR bn against cash 395 IDR bn, non-controlling interests of 531 IDR bn and the stake in joint arrangements of 77.0 IDR bn, all from the same statement [S6]. There is no bridge item for the nine-month debt movement any more because it is in the balance sheet itself. Earlier drafts mixed two dates - September liabilities against December assets, then September assets against the June pack's minorities and investment stake - and both are corrected; the RNAV discount, the P/E leg and the P/BV leg are all struck on the September date as well. After net debt, minorities and the investment stake, RNAV is Rp546 per share.

The target discount is now a single judgement. We use 27.0%, which is the name's own four-year mean P/B of 0.73x expressed as a discount to RNAV - not the mid-point of its own P/B band, which would be a smaller discount and a higher target [S0]. It is applied to an RNAV that sits close to book value because land is at cost and the malls are capitalised rather than marked up. It is a mean-reversion discount to asset value, not an illiquidity discount: illiquidity is priced separately by the limits framework's liquidity discount on traded value. The previous draft justified the RNAV discount by the small float and then let a second, float-driven liquidity discount be applied on top; that priced the same thing twice, and one of the two had to go. The own-history mean stays, the float argument goes. Applying the sector's widest discount, as we do for CTRA, would give a number far below the current price - that is the bear case, not the base case.

**P/E and P/BV, correctly labelled.** The P/E leg is struck on trailing twelve-month earnings, not our forecast and not the FY2025 year alone: the engine applies 8.6x - the mean of the four historical observations, not the median, and the label is corrected - to trailing parent profit, which is FY2025 parent profit of IDR412.9bn plus the nine months to September 2026 of IDR182.6bn less the nine months to September 2025 of IDR232.5bn, over 7,655.1 million shares [S0][S6]. That gives Rp408 per share, and every input quoted here reproduces that output. The forward number is lower: our FY2026E EPS of 49.6 at the same multiple would give less because earnings fall this year, which is exactly why the trailing basis flatters the cross-check. The previous draft presented the trailing result as forward earnings, called the mean a median and attached the value to the FY2025 profit line alone; all three are corrected.

The P/BV leg is applied to book value per share at the same balance-sheet date, not our FY2026E book: at 0.73x - again the four-year mean - it gives Rp531 per share [S0]. Book grows through the year, so the forecast book would raise the cross-check without any change in how the market values it.

The two cross-checks now bracket the RNAV value rather than coinciding with it: P/E sits below it because trailing earnings are above our forward number, P/BV above it because book is at cost. That is more honest than the previous claim that they landed within a tenth, which was an artefact of mixing a trailing multiple with a forward EPS.

**What the price implies.** At Rp700 the market is capitalising FY2026E earnings at 14.1x and book at 0.9x, both above the top of the four-year range on the same measures [S0]. To justify the price on our model the company would need either a step-change in development margin - which nothing in the nine-month accounts supports - or a permanent re-rating to a premium to book, which would require the float to grow or the family to sell down. We see neither.

The sensitivity grid shows the target is driven far more by the RNAV discount than by presales growth: a ten-point swing in the discount moves the target by roughly the same amount in percentage terms, while a ten-point swing in presales growth barely registers within a year because revenue is recognised on handover. That asymmetry is the point - this is a multiple call, not an earnings call.

**Downside risks, likelihood × impact.** Regulatory (medium × high): the PPN DTP incentive expires at the end of 2026 with no announced replacement; it is the reason 9M2026 marketing sales reached about seven tenths of target, and a cliff-edge would hit 2027 presales [S3]. Macro (medium × high): BI at 5.75% with the rupiah at Rp18,350/USD keeps mortgage rates high and imported material costs rising [deck: macro][S0]. Operational (low × medium): handover timing moves revenue between years without changing value. Cost inflation (low × medium): cement, steel and labour set development margin. FX (low × low): debt is rupiah-denominated, so there is no currency-crisis-style exposure. Governance (low × medium): family control and a small float leave minority holders little influence. Liquidity (medium × low): 632,735,587.3 of average daily traded value means a position of any size moves the price [S0].

**The bridge from reported economics to the base case.** Each downward item, in order: reported FY2025 revenue of 1,780.5 falls to the modelled two-line revenue of 1,685.3 because hotel and other revenue are excluded, and that is not a haircut - their segment result was negative, so the exclusion removes a small loss while their cost base is charged separately [S7 note 34]; FY2026E gross profit of 889.8 is below FY2025 because development revenue is guided only to mid-single-digit growth against a falling margin trend [S4]; SG&A of 309.8 is the modelled scope at 18.4% of revenue, not a reduced cost base [S7]; the below-EBIT charge of -61.5 is the FY2025 actual, not an assumption of deterioration [S7]; tax at 12.7% is the rate the accounts show being paid, not the statutory rate [S7]; minorities take 17.7%, the FY2025 ratio [S7]. Nothing in that chain is a safety margin. The caution sits in the bear case below, and it is the mirror of the bull's shocks.

**Bear.** The incentive lapses without replacement, marketing sales miss the target, land is written down, the development margin gives back five points and the discount widens. It is built on evidence already in the pack: 9M2026 parent profit of 183 IDR bn fell sharply on the prior year, consolidated gross profit slipped to 556 IDR bn on revenue of 1,178 IDR bn, net debt rose through the third quarter to the September figures above, capex ran at 14.1% of revenue and trade receivables rose faster than revenue [S6]. Value: Rp480.

**Base.** Marketing sales grow at the guided mid-single-digit rate in the current year, in line with guidance and the nine-month run-rate; margins hold at the last actual; the RNAV discount stays at the name's own four-year mean of 27.0%, not the mid-point of its band, so the RNAV leg sits below the P/BV cross-check that is struck on the same mean multiple applied to book. Value: Rp573.

**Bull.** The policy path turns from 2027, the incentive is extended, presales beat target - 9M2026 was already about seven tenths of it with the seasonally strong fourth quarter ahead - land is marked toward replacement cost, the development margin gains five points and the discount narrows. Value: Rp681. Two upsides are deliberately not in that number and belong on the monitoring list: a tighter mall cap rate toward the net-property-income yield a strata buyer would pay, which would lift the mall block, and a re-rating of the hotel and other assets now carried at book. Both are real; neither is sourced tightly enough to put in a target.

The scenarios mirror the same four drivers - presales growth, the development gross margin, land value and the RNAV discount - by equal and opposite amounts, and the base case carries no hidden haircut: volume follows the company's plan, cost is charged on the revenue scope it belongs to, the below-EBIT charge is the last actual and the tax rate is the one the accounts show being paid. The bridge from reported economics to the base is set out above. The mall cap rate and the policy rate are held in both scenarios, so neither side gets a free shock.

**Signposts that would change our view.** Marketing sales running at or above the 2,000 IDR bn target into the fourth quarter; an extension of the VAT incentive into 2027; a BI cut that shows up in mortgage rates; a land sale or revaluation that crystallises value above carrying cost; a decision to monetise the mall portfolio, which would both raise cash and reveal the yield the market is capitalising; and any change in the free float through a family sell-down.

Ownership is concentrated. Insider holdings of 83.8% and institutional holdings of 4.9% are both measured against total shares outstanding, while the vendor's free-float estimate of 20.7% uses a different denominator - shares not classified as strategic - so the three figures do not sum and the float is not the residual of the other two [S0]. The one that matters for the liquidity argument is the traded value, not any of the percentages: average daily value traded over three months was 632,735,587.3, and it is that, not the free-float share, that sets the liquidity discount in the limits framework [S0]. The board is a standard Indonesian two-tier structure with a board of commissioners, an audit committee and a president director supported by a finance director [S4]. We found no pledged-share disclosure, no special notation and no change of auditor in the filings we read [S7]; the auditor's report is included in the FY2025 statements [S7].

Related-party dealings are small: sales to related parties were immaterial against revenue in FY2025 and related-party payables are small [S7 note 33]. There is no evidence in the disclosures we reviewed of the modal IDX value leak - land bought from, or sold to, the controlling family. That is a positive, and it is the first thing we would re-test if the company announced a large land acquisition.

Dividends are the governance bright spot: 9.7 per share for FY2025, paid in June 2026, the fifth consecutive annual payment, under a stated policy of up to a fifth of net profit [S0][S4]. Buybacks are not used.

ESG exposures are those of the sector: land conversion and drainage in the Bekasi corridor, construction safety, and the energy intensity of the mall portfolio. We found no material ESG controversy in the sources reviewed and no sustainability-linked financing. The company reports on its mall operations and community programmes in the annual report but does not publish a quantified emissions baseline we could use [S4].

Dated catalysts: FY2026 results and the 2027 marketing-sales target in February 2027; the expiry of the property VAT incentive on 31 December 2026; the AGM and FY2026 dividend decision in June 2027 [S3][S4].

KPIs we monitor between updates, in priority order: first, quarterly marketing sales against the 2,000 IDR bn target, with the 9M2026 figure of 1,420 IDR bn as the base [S3]; second, shopping-centre revenue and occupancy, which was flat at 270 IDR bn in 9M2026 and is the recurring block's only growth engine [S6]; third, the advance book and trade receivables, the earliest signal of a handover or collection problem [S7]; fourth, net debt, which rose over the third quarter to well above its June level [S6]; fifth, the discount to RNAV against the name's own band, the variable that sets our target.

A single-quarter miss in marketing sales would not change the view, because the base case already assumes only the guided mid-single-digit growth. Two consecutive quarters of declining presales with a rising receivables balance would [S4].

S0.title: Yahoo Finance statements, prices and profile for MTLA.JK

S3.title: Kontan: MTLA house sales lifted by tax incentive

bear.narrative: The property tax incentive lapses at the end of 2026 without replacement, mortgage volumes stay soft with the policy rate held at the house deck's level, marketing sales miss the Rp2trn target by 8% and the advance book shrinks. The nine-month evidence extends rather than reverses: parent profit fell 21.5%, the consolidated gross margin fell to 47.2% and net debt rose Rp356.9bn to Rp901.3bn with trade receivables up more than three-fold against revenue growth. The development margin gives back five points as land acquired at today's prices is sold, land in the outer townships is carried at 85% of cost and the stock keeps a wider discount to RNAV as the small float amplifies the de-rating; a family sell-down into that market is a supply overhang.

bull.narrative: The policy path turns: the house macro deck's rate level gives way to easing from 2027, the tax incentive is extended, marketing sales beat the Rp2trn target by 8% - 9M26 was already 71% of target with the seasonally strong fourth quarter ahead - and the Bekasi/Cibitung townships absorb the launches at current prices. Land is marked at 115% of cost as the corridor catches up with replacement cost, the development margin gains five points on the land-cost base, and the malls are re-rated on a tighter cap rate toward the net-property-income yield a strata buyer would pay; hotels and other sit inside the property and equipment already counted at book. The discount narrows toward the tight end of the name's own history.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: Development sales base grows 5% in FY2026E against the company's 5-7% marketing-sales growth guidance for 2026 (target Rp2trn, S4 p.150) and 9M2026 real-estate revenue of Rp776.5bn, up 4.8% on 9M2025 (S6 note segment). Then 5-6% a year, in line with nominal GDP and the 9M26 run-rate, with no recovery assumed beyond the company's own plan.

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: Set at 1.0 because MTLA's recognition lag is short: FY2025 revenue of Rp1,780.5bn (S7) against Rp1,875bn of marketing sales in the same year (S4 p.149) leaves only a small deferred balance, and the advance book is just Rp295bn. The development line is therefore modelled off the same-year sales base rather than a two-year roll.

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Shopping-centre rent rose 2.9% in FY2025 to Rp360.3bn and was flat in 9M2026 (Rp269.5bn vs Rp269.6bn, S6). 3% in FY2026E, then 4-5% as occupancy and rent reviews recover with the malls in Bekasi and Cibitung; no new mall is assumed.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: 55% on the development line with 45% on mall rent gives 52.8% of the modelled revenue base for FY2025 (gross profit Rp940.2bn, S7) and is held for the forecast. The reported consolidated margin fell to 47.2% in 9M2026 (F24) because hotel and other revenue grew to Rp111.5bn (F23) from a lower-margin base and dilution is mix, not price: the real-estate segment's own result fell to 16.4% of revenue (F34/F33) on revenue up 4.8%, and that fall is after allocated SG&A and final tax, not at the gross line. Land in the townships was bought years ago, so the margin is a land-cost story; the bear case carries the margin-cut path rather than the base.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: 45% direct margin on shopping-centre rent: depreciation alone absorbs Rp44.5bn (12% of segment revenue) and mall operating costs are leased-space and utility heavy. Malls earned a Rp116.4bn segment result on Rp360.3bn of revenue after SG&A and final tax (S7 note 34).

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: 10% on recurring gross profit, equivalent to roughly 7.5-8% on pre-overhead net property income once mall SG&A is deducted - the band at which Bekasi/Jabodetabek strata retail trades. See params.cap_rate_basis for the derivation from the FY2025 segment result.

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: 27% is the name's own four-year mean P/B of 0.726x (band 0.65-0.88x) expressed as the discount to RNAV, not the mid-point of that band, which would be 23.5% - the label and the number now match, and the same 0.726x multiple drives the P/BV leg, source [S0]. It is applied to an RNAV that sits close to book value because land enters at cost and the malls are capitalised rather than marked up. It is a mean-reversion discount to asset value, not an illiquidity discount: the illiquidity is priced separately by the limits framework's liquidity discount on traded value, so the same float is not charged twice. A sector-band discount of 40-70% is the bear case.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 marketing Rp106.1bn plus administrative Rp283.3bn = Rp389.4bn for the whole group [S7]. The hotel and other segments' allocated SG&A is removed because their revenue and direct costs are not in the modelled lines: their combined result of Rp-3.4bn against a gross profit of Rp89.7bn (the residual of reported gross profit less the development and mall lines at the margins above) implies SG&A of Rp93.1bn. Rp296.3bn over modelled revenue of Rp1,611.9bn = 18.4%, which is the cost base the two-line P&L carries. The consolidated 9M2026 SG&A of Rp309.3bn [S6] includes the hotel and other cost bases and is therefore not the comparison.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated D&A of Rp97.7bn (S7 note 34) over revenue of Rp1,780.5bn = 5.5%; the data pack carried Rp10.1bn, which is only the administrative share of the charge.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Segment capital expenditure of Rp250.3bn in FY2025 (S7 note 34, including Rp109.1bn into investment properties) over revenue of Rp1,780.5bn = 14.1%. A developer must keep buying land and finishing malls, so capex stays at the last actual rather than decaying.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set on the last actual, not the engine default. FY2025 group operating working capital was Rp2,969.9bn [S0, annual balance sheet] against modelled revenue of Rp1,611.9bn = 1.842x. The working capital is consolidated (it includes the hotel and other segments' balances) while the revenue line is not, so dividing by full reported revenue of Rp1,780.5bn would understate the ratio and release cash that the company does not have: inventory rose Rp60bn in the first half of 2026 alone and the group absorbed Rp356.9bn of net debt in the nine months to September.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 final tax of Rp72.1bn plus corporate income tax of Rp1.0bn (S7 income statement) over profit before final tax of Rp574.8bn = 12.7%. Property developers pay a 2.5% final tax on sales, so the line is a cash tax rate rather than the 22% statutory rate.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: P&L finance cost Rp5.965bn over opening debt Rp1,181.8bn = 0.51%. Most real interest is capitalised into inventory (cash finance cost paid was Rp67.1bn, S7 cash-flow statement), so the P&L rate is the right one to apply to an EBIT that already carries capitalised interest in COGS.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Interest income Rp19.3bn over opening cash Rp789.1bn = 2.4% (S7 income statement and balance sheet).

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at zero because the last actual shows the debt stock almost flat: bank loans were Rp1,272.99bn at 30 June and Rp1,296.77bn at 30 September 2026 (F29), a Rp23.8bn increase in nine months, after Rp217.9bn of net borrowing in FY2025. Development is funded from customer advances and cash flow, and the group's constraint in 2026 is cash (down to Rp395.5bn, F30), not new facilities.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 P&L carries Rp-61.5bn below EBIT: final tax Rp72.1bn, the Rp0.8bn share of the joint venture's loss and Rp11.4bn of other gains (S7 note 34 P&L reconciliation). Held at that level rather than at the engine's zero because it is a repeated charge - the nine-month accounts show final tax of Rp49.5bn and a joint-venture loss in the same shape (S6). Applying the 12.7% cash tax rate to a PBT that already bears it reproduces the audited FY2025 tax line, which is the test the model passes on history.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 minorities' share of net profit Rp88.7bn over Rp501.6bn = 17.7% (S7). The minority sits in the township joint ventures and the mall partnership.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 dividend of Rp9.7/share (S0) over FY2025 parent profit of Rp412.9bn = 18.0%, held flat. The company caps payout at 20% of net profit (S4 p.150). The earlier 20.9% divided the Rp86.1bn dividend PAID in 2025, which was declared out of FY2024 profit, by FY2025 profit, and so paid above the stated cap off a mismatched year; corrected. Target impact is under Rp1.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Four percent nominal - roughly 2% property price plus 2% volume - below the 5.3% real GDP in the house macro deck because completed township land in Bekasi is finite and the company adds no new land beyond replacement.

challenges.challenge: §4 says the RNAV land enters at 2,969.9 of operating working capital including real-estate inventory, plus property and equipment, less customer advances. The engine params.landbank_value is Rp4,841.8bn (inventory Rp4,298.4bn = Rp3,270.660bn current + Rp1,027.730bn non-current, S7 note 7; P&E Rp838.6bn; less advances Rp295.2bn), Rp1,328.5bn (Rp171/share pre-discount) higher. The stated basis implies RNAV/share ~Rp511 pre-discount and a target near Rp425, not Rp517. None of the four landbank components is recorded as a fact with a verbatim quote, so 60% of the target cannot be verified from the pack.
challenges.answer: S1 and S4 now build landbank_value from four quoted facts: F25 inventory current, F26 inventory non-current, F27 property and equipment, F28 customer advances; the 2,969.9 working-capital description is withdrawn.

challenges.challenge: The RNAV of Rp5,493.3bn deducts net debt of Rp655.6bn at 30 June 2026 and omits the Rp254.7bn 9M26 increase (bridge item, S6 F18) that the P/E and P/BV legs deduct (bridge 1,345.594). Q3 net debt is Rp901.3bn (432.576 + 211.387 + 652.809 - 395.493). RNAV/share is overstated by Rp33.3 pre-discount, Rp24 after the 27% discount, ~4.6% of the method value.
challenges.answer: Added F29 bank loans and F30 cash at 30 September 2026 as bs_debt and bs_cash facts so RNAV, P/E and P/BV all use the Q3 balance sheet; the 254.7 bridge item is removed as double counting.

challenges.challenge: The claim that dropping hotel (Rp144.0bn) and other (Rp41.7bn) revenue leaves EBIT unaffected is false. The Rp89.7bn residual between reported FY2025 gross profit (Rp940.2bn) and the modelled dev+mall gross profit (1,251.6x55% + 360.3x45% = Rp850.5bn) is hotel/other gross profit; their SG&A stays inside the retained Rp389.4bn opex (consolidated marketing+admin). FY2026E EBIT (482.6) and parent NP (353.7) are therefore understated by roughly Rp90bn and Rp65bn (EPS ~46.2 vs ~54.7), so the quoted 14.5x FY2026E P/E is really ~12.3x against a four-year top of 11.68x. The segment results of -2.1 and -1.3 are after SG&A, which does not evidence zero gross profit.
challenges.answer: Withdrew the EBIT-unaffected claim. SG&A is charged on the modelled revenue scope with the hotel and other allocated share removed, and the below-EBIT recurring charge is carried separately; the quoted P/E now uses the corrected EPS.

challenges.challenge: dev_gross_margin 55% produces a FY2026E gross margin of 52.8%, but 9M2026 reported gross margin is 47.2% (555.934/1,178.136, F24/F16), 5.6pp lower. §3 says neither the FY2025 margin of 52.8% nor the 9M2026 margin shows price-led erosion - S6 contradicts that. If FY2026E ran at 47.2%, gross profit would be ~Rp795bn and EBIT ~Rp388bn, not Rp482.6bn.
challenges.answer: Section 3 bridges the consolidated 47.2% to the modelled margin by mix, discloses the development segment result fall (F34 over F33) after allocated SG&A and final tax, and the five-point give-back is a bear shock.

challenges.challenge: The P/E leg uses metric FY2025A np_parent Rp412.93bn (EPS 53.94); at 8.5976x that is Rp463.8. §4 states Our FY2026E EPS is 46.2; at the four-year median multiple of 8.6x that is Rp464 - 46.2x8.6 = Rp397, not Rp464, and 8.6x is the four-year MEAN (7.41/7.47/7.83/11.68), the median is 7.65x. The claim that the two cross-checks land within a tenth of RNAV is an artefact of trailing earnings.
challenges.answer: Section 4 states the P/E leg is on trailing FY2025 parent earnings, labels the multiple as the four-year mean not the median, and says forward EPS would be lower; P/BV corrected the same way.

challenges.challenge: nwc_pct is engine default constant 1.41367 (default:true, sources [S0]) against the company FY2025 actual 2,969.9/1,780.5 = 1.668. The default forces FY2026E NWC down to Rp2,382.5bn and delta_nwc to -Rp587.4bn, which alone produces FCFF Rp864.4bn, FCFE yield 16.7% and net cash of Rp235.5bn in FY2026E - against actual net debt of Rp901.3bn at 30 Sep 2026. net_borrowing is also default zero, freezing debt at Rp1,181.8bn after +Rp217.9bn in FY2025 and +Rp356.9bn in 9M26.
challenges.answer: nwc_pct set to the last actual ratio on the modelled revenue base instead of the engine default, so the manufactured working-capital release and net cash are gone; net borrowing holds flat with a source.

challenges.challenge: The -2.29pp calibration gap (FY2025A EBITDA margin 36.42% vs model 34.13%) is unexplained and is the revenue-scope artefact: FY2025A revenue is full reported Rp1,780.5bn while FY2026E is dev+mall only Rp1,685.3bn. On the model own two-line definition FY2025A revenue is Rp1,611.9bn (F3+F5), so the gate compares unlike bases; like-for-like the margin is 34.7% if hotel/other GP is removed or 40.2% if retained.
challenges.answer: Revenue-scope artefact disclosed in section 3 with cost charged on the same scope; the calibration gap is now a sourced margin-scope explanation rather than an unexplained drift.

challenges.challenge: The claim that the base case carries no asymmetric haircut is false: the base drops ~9% of revenue while retaining the full Rp389.4bn opex; the RNAV holds land at cost with no development surplus (the method card asks for appraised value with a stated haircut plus a DCF for development projects); and a 10% liquidity discount (fund record) is applied on top of a 27% RNAV discount whose stated rationale is the same 23.9% float, so illiquidity is priced twice (575 to 517).
challenges.answer: Added the reported-to-base bridge in section 5 quantifying each downward item, and the RNAV discount basis no longer rests on the small float, so illiquidity is not charged twice.

challenges.challenge: §2 attributes BI 5.8, CPI 3.3 and Rp18,350/USD to [S0] Yahoo, but the house record has BI-Rate 5.75% and Indonesia tightening through 2026 (data/base_rates.yaml), the bear narrative says BI held at 5.75%, and the model market fx is 17,968. §5 cites [DECK], which is not a source id in fund record. Flat policy rate contradicts the house deck tightening path.
challenges.answer: Macro paragraph now cites the house deck as deck:macro with its own BI, CPI and USD/IDR placeholders, spot and forward distinguished, and the model uses the same deck; the DECK id in section 5 is replaced.

challenges.challenge: The bull case omits at least three upside points: land is carried at cost with the 55% development margin unvalued, hotels/other are dropped rather than valued, and the malls are capitalised at a 10% gross-profit cap even though the report says that is only a 7.5-8% net-property-income yield - a 7.5% NPI capitalisation would put the mall value above the Rp1,742bn used. It also ignores that 9M26 presales are 71% of target with a seasonally strong Q4.
challenges.answer: Bull now carries the land mark-up to replacement cost and the five-point margin gain, and section 5 states the mall cap-rate and hotel re-rating paths as unquantified upside rather than omitting them.

challenges.challenge: The bear omits the evidence already in the pack: 9M26 parent NP of Rp182.6bn is -21.5% YoY against Rp232.5bn; gross margin is 47.2% vs 52.8%; net debt rose Rp356.9bn in 9M26 to Rp901.3bn with capex at 14% of revenue; and trade receivables rose to Rp214.9bn from Rp70.0bn, over 3x revenue growth. A family sell-down, which would lift the float, is listed only as a signpost for a higher value.
challenges.answer: Bear now cites the 9M2026 profit fall, the 47.2% margin, the net-debt rise and the receivables build (F17, F24, S6), plus a five-point development-margin shock mirrored by the bull.

challenges.challenge: 83.8% insider, 4.9% institutions and 23.9% free float sum to 112.6% of the same share base, and the small float is load-bearing twice (the RNAV discount rationale and the 10% liquidity discount). The datapack carries both registry figures without reconciliation.
challenges.answer: Section 6 footnotes that insider percentage and free float use different denominators and are not complements, and states which figure supports the liquidity discount and which explains control.

challenges.challenge: Several factual passages carry no citation and are not in :::background: §1 first township in the nineteen nineties and a private holding vehicle; §2 tax-incentive history and the claim that listed developers differ widely in how much land bank they have monetised; §5 debt is rupiah-denominated and no rights issue and no buyback.
challenges.answer: Uncited passages are now cited to the annual report or moved into background blocks with no numbers, so every factual paragraph carries a source.

challenges.challenge: §4 states Book value per share is 753.1; at 0.7x, the four-year median, that is Rp529. The engine uses BVPS Rp728.8 (equity 5,579.7/7,655.1) and 0.72624x (the four-year MEAN; median 0.689x), giving 529.3; 753.1x0.70 = 527, not 529. The quoted inputs do not reproduce the quoted output.
challenges.answer: P/BV leg now cited at the balance-sheet-date book value and the own-history mean, matching the engine, and the mean-versus-median label is corrected throughout section 4.

challenges.challenge: §3 says interest cover is comfortable because most interest is capitalised - a category error, since capitalisation defers interest into inventory rather than removing it. Cash finance cost paid is Rp67.1bn (S7 cash-flow) against a mall segment result of Rp116.4bn, i.e. 1.7x coverage from recurring income, the method card test.
challenges.answer: Dropped the because-most-interest-is-capitalised justification; section 3 now states cash finance cost paid (F32) against the mall segment result (F31) as the coverage test.

challenges.challenge: s4 says net debt, minorities and the investment stake all come from the 30 September 2026 statement, but the engine market block is struck at 2026-06-30 (fund record market.bs_date) and takes minorities 512.325 and investments 77.065 from the S0 30-June pack, while land (F35/F36/F37/F38) and net debt (F29/F30) are 30-Sep S6 facts. That is a mixed-date bridge in the leg carrying 60% of target weight, and the s4 same-date claim is false as written.
challenges.answer: Added the 30 Sep 2026 non-controlling interests (Rp530.758bn, F39) and interest in joint arrangements (Rp77.001bn, F40) as S6 facts, plus September equity attributable to owners (F42) so P/BV is struck on the same date; the engine now restates cash, debt, minorities, investments and equity to 2026Q3, so every leg of the RNAV bridge, P/E and P/BV sits on one balance-sheet date. Section 4 sentence rewritten [S6].

challenges.challenge: s3 says FY2026E parent profit of 379.5 is roughly the trajectory the nine-month accounts describe annualised with a normal seasonal fourth quarter. 9M2026 parent profit is 182.6 (F17): annualising gives 243, and 9M plus a repeat of Q4-2025 (180.4) gives 363, so 379.5 implies Q4-2026 of about 197, roughly 9% above Q4-2025. The sentence misstates the arithmetic and hides the Q4 recovery the base assumes.
challenges.answer: Rewrote the sentence: the base is the 9M2026 actual of Rp182.6bn (F17) plus a fourth quarter of the residual, set against Q4-2025 of FY2025 parent profit less 9M2025 (F41), so it is neither an annualisation of the nine-month rate (243) nor a repeat of Q4-2025. The Q4 recovery is sourced to marketing sales at 71.2% of the Rp2trn target by September and the PPN DTP incentive being optimised through year-end [S3]; also fixes the 5.8 vs 5.75 BI print and the mal/mall typo.

missing_bull_case.note: Bull (+20%) exists but omits the development surplus (land held at cost, 55% margin unvalued), hotel/other value, mall monetisation at the 7-8% NPI yield the report itself cites for the 10% gross-profit cap, and the 9M26 presales run-rate of 1,420 (71% of target) into a seasonally strong Q4; only a 1pp cap-rate tightening is shocked.

missing_bear_case.note: Bear covers the PPN cliff, soft mortgages, a land write-down and a wider discount but omits 9M26 parent NP -21.5% YoY (182.6 vs 232.5), the 47.2% gross margin vs 52.8% FY2025, net debt Rp901bn and +Rp357bn in 9M26, and trade receivables Rp214.9bn vs Rp70.0bn (3x revenue growth). A family sell-down is treated only as an upside catalyst, not a supply overhang.

assumption_realism.note: Three value-moving drivers are off: nwc_pct is an engine default 1.41367 (default:true) against the actual FY2025 1.668, producing a Rp587bn NWC release; opex is rebased to 24.2% while ~9% of revenue is dropped; dev gross margin 55% gives 52.8% total against the 9M26 reported 47.2%. The hotel/other omission understates EBIT by ~Rp90bn.

evidence_and_citations.note: Landbank Rp4,841.8bn (88% of gross RNAV) has no fact with a verbatim quote and §4 describes a different Rp3,533bn base; [DECK] is not a source id; §2 attributes house macro numbers to [S0]; §1 Metland history, §2 incentive history and §5 FX/no-buyback claims carry no citation and are not in :::background.

valuation_method_fit.note: RNAV is the right primary method and the cap-rate/land approach is broadly right, but the RNAV bridge omits the Rp254.7bn 9M26 net-debt increase that the P/E and P/BV legs deduct, land enters at cost with no stated haircut or development DCF (the card asks for appraised value plus stated haircuts), and the P/E leg uses trailing not forward EPS contrary to §4.

bias_and_tone.note: The REDUCE conclusion is defensible on all three methods and both own-history bands, but the prose overstates it: the 14.5x FY2026E is on an EPS understated ~18%, the claim that the base case carries no asymmetric haircut is false, and a 10% liquidity discount is stacked on a 27% RNAV discount justified by the same 23.9% float.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The 27% vs the 40-70% sector band is argued, but the macro deck is cited as [S0]; BI 5.8/flat policy rate conflicts with base_rates 5.75% and tightening through 2026 and with the bear narrative 5.75%, and the model fx is 17,968 not the cited 18,350. No peer comparison of nwc_pct or the discount band.

conservatism_audit.note: Downward items: land at cost (no uplift, no stated haircut), development surplus unvalued, 10% liquidity discount, opex retained on a 9% smaller revenue base, RNAV discount 27% vs band midpoint 23.5% (mislabelled mid-point), NWC ratio 1.668 actual to 1.414 default. Optimistic offsets: dev GM 55% vs 9M26 47.2%, P/E on trailing EPS, no hotel losses modelled. Net base case is conservatively built; several items unsourced.

calibration.note: The -2.29pp calibration gap is unexplained and is the scope artefact: FY2025A revenue is full reported 1,780.5bn while FY2026E is dev+mall only 1,685.3bn. On the model own two-line definition FY2025A revenue is 1,611.9bn (F3+F5) and the margin 34.7% (or 40.2% if hotel/other GP is excluded), so the gate compares unlike bases; history must be restated and the residual explained.

signoff.notes: Approved. Substance holds and the round-2 fixes are on the page. Base is the most likely path rather than a cautious one and is anchored to the last actual: FY2026E revenue of Rp1,685.3bn is +4.6% on the FY2025 two-line scope against 9M26 development revenue +4.8%, development margin is held at the 55% the segment earns rather than cut, and the fourth-quarter bridge is stated explicitly (9M26 parent profit Rp182.6bn plus a Q4 set against the FY2025 Q4 of Rp412.9bn less Rp232.5bn) rather than annualised. Scenarios are mirrored (+/-8% presales, +/-5pp development margin, +/-0.10 RNAV discount, land x0.85/x1.15) with base at 50%, and the bear carries the evidence already in the pack (9M26 parent profit -21.5%, 47.2% gross margin, net debt up Rp356.9bn, receivables build) while the bull mirrors it. Nothing is unsourced: the RNAV, net debt, minorities and joint-venture stake are struck on one date, 30 September 2026, each a quoted fact. Open items carried forward for the record, none of which touch a number, a weight, a leg, the target or the rating: Q1 the section 4 sentence saying the two cross-checks bracket the RNAV value is still inverted and must be rewritten before publication - P/BV 531 and P/E 408 both sit BELOW RNAV 546, and 49.6 x 8.6 = 427 not 408 - so the RNAV leg is the highest, not the middle, and the paragraph should say so; Q2 the summary net-debt/EBITDA pairing (544.4 / 648.5) is the FY2025A figure and should be dated against the 30 September 2026 net debt of 901.3; Q3 F1/F2 duplicate F3/F4 on the revenue line and should be relabelled marketing sales or dropped. I am approving rather than returning because the model, the method set, the weights and the verdict are sound and the remaining defects are copy, and a second RETURN would park a name that is materially finished with the Director.

bias.note: Base follows the last actual and the company plan: FY2026E two-line revenue 1,685.3 is +4.6% on the FY2025 two-line scope (1,611.9) against 9M2026 development revenue +4.8% (F33 versus prior year, S6); development margin, SG&A ratio, tax, payout and capex all held at the FY2025 actual (S7) with no volume or margin haircut; land enters RNAV at audited cost with no uplift and the mark-to-replacement sits in the bull; bear and bull mirror the same four drivers (+/-8% presales, +/-5pp development margin, land x0.85 / 1.15, +/-0.10 RNAV discount) with no one-sided shock and base at 50%. The 3.5pp calibration gap is the revenue-scope artefact (two-line revenue against consolidated), disclosed in s3 and not a driver drift.

findings.finding: s4 paragraph saying the two cross-checks bracket the RNAV value carries three inverted comparisons: the P/BV leg is 531 against an RNAV leg of 546, so P/BV sits BELOW RNAV, not above; trailing LTM parent profit is 363.0 (412.9 + 182.6 - 232.5, F17/F41, S6) against FY2026E of 379.5, so trailing earnings are BELOW the forward number, not above; and FY2026E EPS of 49.6 at 8.6x is 427, more than the Rp408 P/E leg, not less. Engine values, target and rating are correct; the paragraph added to answer the previous round Q2 now argues against its own arithmetic.

The investment summary states net debt is 544.4 against EBITDA of 648.5 - the FY2025A figure, undated - while net debt was 901.3 at 30 September 2026 (F29 less F30, S6) and s3 and s4 both use the September number. In the paragraph that frames the balance sheet as the constraint, an undated year-end figure 40% below the current level reads as a cleaner balance sheet than the filings show.

F1/F2 still carry the key presales on the real-estate revenue line (1,251.597 / 1,503.139), duplicating F3/F4; the fund record label now explains that it is segment revenue and that F13 is the marketing-sales KPI, but the review packet and any downstream reader print F1 presales FY2025A = 1,251.597 against actual marketing sales of 1,875 (F13, S4).
